papers_read.title_as_printed: Associations between brain structures, cognition and dual-task performance in patients with mild cognitive impairment: A study based on voxel-based morphology (Cheng et al., Human Movement Science 97 (2024) 103257)

Curve Walking Reveals More Gait Impairments in Older Adults with Mild Cognitive Impairment than Straight Walking: A Kinect Camera-Based Study (Seifallahi, Galvin, Ghoraani; J Alzheimers Dis Rep 8 (2024) 423-435)

what_each_reports.P-687: 30 MCI vs 30 HC (Guangzhou). Single-task TUG (10 m to a table and back) 17.29 +/- 2.34 vs 17.60 +/- 2.89 s, p = 0.643; dual-task TUG (dialling an 11-digit number while walking back) 29.23 +/- 8.02 vs 24.92 +/- 4.42 s, p = 0.012; dialling accuracy 70.0% vs 86.7%, p = 0.117. Right cerebellar anterior lobe GMV correlates with dual-task time r = -0.32, p = 0.012.
what_each_reports.P-1082: 25 MCI vs 30 HC (IDAA, Semnan, Iran), Kinect v.2, single-task 10 m straight and oval-path walking, 50 markers, ANCOVA-adjusted. Straight: velocity 47.39 vs 50.13 cm/s, p = 0.780; cadence p = 0.247; 20/50 markers significant (none macro). Curve: velocity 39.27 vs 45.90 cm/s, p = 0.007; cadence p = 0.018; 27/50 significant. ROC AUC 0.83 (curve) vs 0.78 (straight) using significant markers.

quantity_a: Group difference in TUG completion time, MCI vs HC, single-task vs cognitive dual-task (phone dialling), Chinese clinic/community sample.
quantity_b: Group differences in Kinect gait markers (velocity, cadence, micro markers), MCI vs HC, single-task straight vs single-task curved-path walking, Iranian sample.
incompatible_if_same: No. The two papers point the same way: in each, the simpler condition shows no MCI-HC difference on the macro time/speed measure (TUG time p = 0.643; straight velocity p = 0.780) and the more demanding condition does (dual-task TUG p = 0.012; curve velocity p = 0.007). There is no disagreement between them to resolve.

gates.task: registry mismatch (T4 vs T1); both are case-control group comparisons, P-1082 adds a descriptive ROC analysis.
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: Sun Yat-sen University clinic/community (China) vs IDAA clients (Iran).
gates.validation_tier: n/a for P-687 (no model); P-1082's ROC is in-sample. Counted as not decisive.
gates.modality_family: both gait/mobility, but instruments differ (stopwatch TUG time vs Kinect joint tracking) and the added demand differs (secondary cognitive task vs curved path, still single-task).

endpoint_and_metric: compatible in direction, not in estimand: TUG completion time vs walking velocity/cadence and micro markers; the 'loaded' condition is a cognitive dual task in P-687 and a curved path without a secondary task in P-1082.
performance_validity: not a performance comparison between the pair (P-687 reports no discrimination metric; P-1082's AUC 0.83/0.78 is not set against anything in P-687).
independence: Distinct cohorts, countries and author teams; independent.
grounds: The record labels both P-687 and P-1082 as the same 'load-necessary arm', so it describes no disagreement between the two papers of the pair.
On the PDFs the two results agree in direction: no MCI-HC difference in the simpler condition and a significant difference under the more demanding condition in each study.

The contradiction the record actually discusses is between these two studies and P-761/P-695 (unloaded gait positives), which are not this pair and are described in the record itself as failing every gate.
P-1082's added demand is a curved path during single-task walking, not a cognitive dual task, so even the shared 'loading' label overstates the overlap with P-687.

evidence_quotes.quote: There was no significant difference in the single task execution time between the MCI and HC groups (MCI: 17.29 ± 2.34 s, HC: 17.60 ± 2.89 s, t = 0.47, p = 0.643).
However, a significant difference in the execution time of the dual-task paradigm was observed between the two groups (MCI: 29.23 ± 8.02 s, HC: 24.92 ± 4.42 s, t = −2.58, p = 0.012).

Individuals with MCI showed impaired cognition and dual-task performance. This study may give more evidence for the relationship between the dual-task paradigm and the gray matter volume of the cerebellum.
We employed a Kinect v.2 camera to record the gait of 55 older adults (30 healthy controls, 25 with MCI) during single-task straight and curve walking tests.
Conversely, the SW test revealed significant differences in 20 out of the 50 extracted markers. None of these markers were macro markers
the area under the curve (AUC) for curved path walking (0.83) was significantly higher than for straight path walking (0.78)

record_defects: The record frames P-1082 as 'cognitive-motor LOADING'; the PDF states both conditions were single-task walking, the difference being path shape (straight vs oval).

The record is filed as a conflict between P-687 and P-1082 but argues against a generalisation drawn from both of them jointly, with P-761 and P-695 as the opposing side; the pair itself contains no disagreement.

The record omits that P-1082 reports ROC AUC 0.83 (curve) vs 0.78 (straight), so straight walking still discriminated in-sample; this supports the record's own caution about 'straight walking misses' but is not cited.
The sample-size explanation ('the pattern tracks sample size') is the record's inference; neither PDF tests it.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Nothing within this pair: a genuine candidate would require pairing P-687 or P-1082 with an unloaded-gait study reporting a significant MCI-HC difference on the same measure (e.g. single-task TUG time or straight-walk velocity under a comparable protocol) whose estimate excludes the null in P-687/P-1082; that is a different record.
